headline: Volume-Led Beat; Cost Inflation Weighs on Margins

highlights: Key Points  Strong Volumes; Margins Under Pressure: Balkrishna Industries reported 2QFY27 revenue of Rs34.5bn, up 48.6% YoY, beating NBIE (+19.0%) and consensus (+12.5%), driven by tyre volumes of 91,397MT (+30% YoY on a weak tariff-hit US base) and continued outperformance in India.

Gross margin contracted by 758bps YoY to 42.5% on raw material and freight inflation and a higher India mix, limiting EBITDA growth to 12.7% YoY at Rs5.9bn (margin 17.0%, -542bps YoY), in line with estimates.

Adjusted PAT rose 6.6% YoY to Rs2.83bn but missed NBIE and consensus by 10.8% and 8.5%, respectively, on higher interest and depreciation.  Outlook: Management expects raw material and freight inflation to persist over the next few quarters.

Price hikes of 2-3% (mainly in India) did not fully offset cost inflation in 2QFY27, and higher freight (~6.5% of sales) is yet to be passed through, with export pricing to remain tactical between volume and profitability.
valuation: Management reiterated a long-term EBITDA margin band of 20-25%.  Valuation: BKT’s volume momentum remains strong, with 1HFY27 tyre volumes up 23% YoY, led by sustained outperformance in India, stable Americas, and market-share gains across key geographies.

We maintain our BUY rating with a revised target price of Rs2,874, valuing the stock at 26x Sep-28E EPS. 2QFY27 Results: Balkrishna Industries reported 2QFY27 revenue of Rs34.5bn, up 48.6% YoY and 1.2% QoQ, ahead of NBIE estimates by 19.0% and consensus by 12.5%.

CMP: Rs2,244 | Target Price (TP): Rs2,874 | Upside: 28% 05 November, 2026 Institutional Equities Balkrishna Industries Ltd 2 Carbon Black – Phase II Ramp-Up Underway; Focus Shifts to Third-Party Sales: Carbon black recorded decent YoY revenue growth in 2QFY27, with third-party sales at ~10% of overall business and demand remaining robust.
